canh-phuc-cung-tan-ngu: A brand-new painting of a natural, lived-in, richly furnished room, painted exactly like image 1 (the bedroom): same hand, same brushwork, same soft painterly finish, same natural warm colours, saturation and contrast, same depth with furniture, curtains and objects arranged through the whole room from the foreground to the back. Wide panoramic, eye-level view, summer morning. ROOM: Cảnh Phúc cung chính điện bedroom, the private bedchamber of the imperial consort who heads this palace in ancient China, a real room in daily use: dark rosewood pillars and beams, carved lattice windows at the back opening onto a sunny courtyard garden with a tree and a lotus pond, a carved wooden partition with a round moon-gate opening; at the centre of the room, the large clear main subject, one canopy bed of carved rosewood with pale pink gauze curtains tied back and pale pink silk bedding embroidered with crabapple blossoms, fine jade-green inlay on the bed frame; around it a dressing table with a bronze mirror and a small jewellery box, a small screen painted with crabapple blossoms, round stools with pale pink cushions, hanging palace lanterns with pink tassels, a clothes rack with a pink robe, a vase of crabapple branches, a small tea table, a bookshelf with boxes, slippers and a small basket on the floor. Cảnh Phúc cung signature style, the same in every room of this palace: crabapple blossoms (hải đường) are its flower, painted on the screens, embroidered on the silks and in the vases; motifs of bats among auspicious clouds carved in the beams and furniture; dark rosewood with jade-green inlay and jade ornaments; round-backed rosewood furniture; a round moon-gate opening in a carved partition. TẦN level, the simplest of the three: pretty and noble but modest, plain polished rosewood with a little carving, few ornaments, little gilding. The pale pink accent colour is woven through the bedding, curtains and cushions. No phoenix anywhere (no phoenix carving, embroidery, figure or pendant), no imperial yellow, no golden-yellow fabrics. FLOOR: warm polished wooden floorboards visible between the furniture, no large rug or carpet covering the floor (at most a small mat under the bed step); the canopy bed sits in the central half of the width. LIGHT: soft warm morning daylight from the right, like the light on the girl in image 2, so a person standing in the room looks lit by it. Do not leave the room empty like a stage; it should feel natural and furnished, people will simply be placed in it later.
